name: Band curl
form_cues: Stand on the band with feet hip-width apart.
Keep elbows pinned to your sides as you curl.
Lower slowly against the band's pull.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to finish reps
safety: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session.
notes: Widen your stance to make it harder.

name: Band chest press
form_cues: Anchor the band at chest height behind you.
Stagger your stance and brace your core.
Press straight forward until arms are long, then return slowly.
safety: Secure the anchor point firmly so the band can't slip free.

name: Band pull-apart
form_cues: Hold the band at shoulder height with straight arms.
Pull the band apart until it touches your chest.
Squeeze shoulder blades together, then return slowly.
safety: Use a light band; this should never pinch the front of the shoulder.
notes: Great as a warm-up before pressing.

name: Band pushdown
form_cues: Anchor the band high, over a door or bar.
Keep elbows tucked at your sides.
Push down until arms are straight, then control the return.
common_mistakes: Leaning over to push with body weight
safety: Make sure the door is closed and locked if using a door anchor.

name: Banded lateral walk
form_cues: Place the mini band above the knees or around the ankles.
Sit into a quarter squat with chest up.
Step sideways, keeping tension on the band.
safety: Keep the band flat on the skin so it doesn't roll and pinch.
notes: Band around ankles or feet is harder than above the knees.

name: Band seated row
form_cues: Sit tall with legs long and the band looped around your feet.
Pull handles to your lower ribs.
Squeeze shoulder blades together before releasing slowly.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to cheat the pull
safety: Wrap the band securely around the feet so it can't slip off.

name: Band lat pulldown
form_cues: Anchor the band high and kneel facing it.
Pull elbows down toward your back pockets.
Keep chest tall and return slowly.
safety: Double-check the high anchor is secure before loading it.

name: Band overhead press
form_cues: Stand on the band and hold handles at shoulder height.
Press straight up until arms are locked out.
Keep ribs down and glutes tight.
safety: Stand squarely on the band so it can't slip out from underfoot.

name: Band lateral raise
form_cues: Stand on the band with handles at your sides.
Raise arms out to shoulder height with soft elbows.
Lower slowly and keep shoulders away from ears.
safety: Use a light band; the tension is highest at the top.

name: Band face pull
form_cues: Anchor the band at face height.
Pull the band toward your forehead, elbows high.
Finish with hands beside your ears, thumbs back.
safety: Keep it light and pain-free in the shoulder.

name: Band squat
form_cues: Stand on the band, handles at shoulders.
Sit hips back and down, knees tracking toes.
Drive through the whole foot to stand tall.
safety: Keep the band under the mid-foot so it can't fly out.

name: Band deadlift
form_cues: Stand on the band and hinge to grab the handles.
Keep a flat back and push hips back.
Stand up by driving hips forward.
safety: Keep the band centred under both feet.

name: Band good morning
form_cues: Stand on the band and loop it behind your neck.
Hinge forward with soft knees and a flat back.
Squeeze glutes to return upright.
safety: Pad the band across the upper back, not the neck.

name: Banded glute bridge
form_cues: Lie on your back with the mini band above your knees.
Press knees out against the band.
Drive hips up and squeeze glutes at the top.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
safety: Keep ribs down to protect the lower back.

name: Banded clamshell
form_cues: Lie on your side, knees bent, band above knees.
Keep feet together and open the top knee.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly.
safety: Move only through a pain-free range.

name: Band glute kickback
form_cues: Loop the band around one ankle and anchor it low.
Kick the leg back from the hip, knee slightly bent.
Squeeze the glute without arching your back.
safety: Hold a support to stay balanced.

name: Band overhead triceps extension
form_cues: Anchor the band low behind you, hands overhead.
Keep elbows pointing up and close to your head.
Straighten arms fully, then lower with control.
safety: Make sure the band is secure behind you before loading it.

name: Band chest fly
form_cues: Anchor the band behind you at chest height.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows.
Hug your arms together in front of your chest.
common_mistakes: Letting arms travel too far back
safety: Avoid overstretching the front of the shoulder.

name: Band external rotation
form_cues: Anchor the band at elbow height.
Tuck the elbow at your side, a towel helps.
Rotate the forearm outward, keeping the elbow still.
common_mistakes: Elbow drifting away from the body
safety: Use a light band and stop if you feel pinching.

name: Band internal rotation
form_cues: Anchor the band at elbow height on your working side.
Keep the elbow tucked at 90 degrees.
Rotate the forearm in across your stomach.
safety: Light resistance only; this is a control drill.

name: Monster walk
form_cues: Band around ankles, sit into a quarter squat.
Step diagonally forward and out with each foot.
Keep constant tension; don't let feet come together.
safety: Keep the band flat so it doesn't roll.

name: Band hamstring curl
form_cues: Lie face down with the band anchored low behind you.
Loop it around your ankles and curl heels to glutes.
Lower slowly without lifting hips.
safety: Anchor the band firmly to something heavy and low.

name: Banded push-up
form_cues: Loop the band across your upper back, ends under hands.
Hold a straight line from head to heels.
Press up hard against the band to lockout.
safety: Pin the band securely under your palms before each rep.

name: Band upright row
form_cues: Stand on the band, hands shoulder-width.
Lead with the elbows up to chest height.
Lower slowly and keep the bar path close.
safety: Stop below shoulder height if you feel a pinch.

name: Band straight-arm pulldown
form_cues: Anchor the band high and hinge slightly.
Keep arms straight and sweep hands to your thighs.
Feel the lats squeeze, then return slowly.
safety: Secure the high anchor before loading it.

name: Seated banded hip abduction
form_cues: Sit on the edge of a bench, band above knees.
Push knees out as far as you can.
Hold a second, then return with control.
common_mistakes: Letting feet come off the floor
safety: Keep the band flat on the thighs.

name: Kettlebell swing
form_cues: Hike the bell back high between your thighs.
Snap hips forward and squeeze glutes hard.
Let the bell float to chest height; arms stay relaxed.
common_mistakes: Squatting the swing instead of hinging
safety: Clear the space around you and keep a neutral spine throughout.

name: American kettlebell swing
form_cues: Swing as normal but carry the bell to overhead.
Finish with biceps by ears, bell bottom up.
Keep ribs down; don't arch to reach overhead.
safety: Skip it if you lack full overhead shoulder mobility.
notes: Common in CrossFit; the Russian swing is safer for most people.

name: One-arm kettlebell swing
form_cues: Grip the handle with one hand, free arm relaxed.
Keep shoulders square; resist the twist.
Drive with hips and let the bell float.
safety: Start lighter than your two-hand swing weight.

name: Kettlebell clean
form_cues: Hike the bell back, then drive hips forward.
Keep the elbow close and zip the bell up.
Catch it softly in the rack, wrist straight.
common_mistakes: Bell flipping over and banging the forearm
safety: Learn with a light bell; a bruised forearm means the path is too wide.

name: Kettlebell snatch
form_cues: Swing back and drive hips explosively.
Keep the bell close and punch through at the top.
Lock out overhead with biceps by your ear.
common_mistakes: Letting the bell flop onto the wrist
Pressing it up instead of hip drive
safety: Needs good overhead mobility; drop the bell safely if control is lost.

name: Turkish get-up
form_cues: Keep eyes on the bell and arm locked the whole time.
Move step by step: roll, elbow, hand, bridge, sweep, stand.
Reverse each step slowly to return to the floor.
safety: Practise with a shoe or no weight first; never lose sight of the bell.
notes: Builds shoulder stability through the whole body.

name: Kettlebell overhead press
form_cues: Start with the bell in the rack, forearm vertical.
Squeeze glutes and grip, then press straight up.
Finish with biceps by your ear, then lower to rack.
safety: Brace hard and don't press through shoulder pain.

name: Kettlebell push press
form_cues: Dip a few centimetres by bending the knees.
Drive up with the legs to launch the bell.
Finish the lockout with the arm.
safety: Keep heels down in the dip and control the bell back to the rack.

name: Kettlebell jerk
form_cues: Dip and drive to launch the bell.
Drop under it with a second dip to lock out.
Stand tall with the arm locked before lowering.
safety: Requires solid overhead mobility and wrist position.
notes: A staple of kettlebell sport.

name: Goblet squat
form_cues: Hold the bell by the horns against your chest.
Sit down between your heels, elbows inside knees.
Drive up through the whole foot, chest tall.
safety: Keep heels down; elevate them slightly if ankles are tight.

name: Double kettlebell front squat
form_cues: Clean both bells to the rack, elbows tucked.
Squat to depth keeping the chest up.
Drive up without letting the bells pull you forward.
safety: Clean the bells into position carefully; set them down rather than drop them.

name: Goblet reverse lunge
form_cues: Hold the bell at your chest.
Step back and lower the back knee softly.
Push through the front foot to return.
safety: Use a support nearby if balance is an issue.

name: Goblet Cossack squat
form_cues: Take a very wide stance holding the bell at your chest.
Shift and sit deep into one hip, other leg straight.
Lift the straight-leg toes up and keep the heel down.
safety: Work within your hip range; go only as deep as you can control.

name: Kettlebell windmill
form_cues: Lock the bell overhead, feet angled away from it.
Push the hip out and slide your free hand down the leg.
Keep eyes on the bell and the arm vertical.
common_mistakes: Twisting the chest down to the floor
safety: Start light; stop if the shoulder feels unstable.

name: Kettlebell halo
form_cues: Hold the bell upside down by the horns.
Circle it closely around your head.
Keep ribs down and hips still.
common_mistakes: Circling too far from the head
safety: Use a light bell and move slowly to avoid knocking your head.
notes: Great shoulder warm-up before pressing.

name: Kettlebell deadlift
form_cues: Stand with the bell between your feet.
Push hips back and grip it with a flat back.
Stand tall by driving hips forward.
safety: Keep the bell close to you and the spine neutral.
notes: Teaches the hinge before learning swings.

name: Double kettlebell Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Hold a bell in each hand at your thighs.
Push hips back with soft knees until hamstrings stretch.
Squeeze glutes to stand up.
safety: Keep bells close to the legs throughout.

name: Kettlebell gorilla row
form_cues: Hinge over two bells placed between your feet.
Row one bell to your hip while pressing into the other.
Alternate sides without twisting the torso.
safety: Keep a flat back and hips high throughout.

name: Kettlebell floor press
form_cues: Lie on the floor, upper arm resting on the ground.
Press the bell up over your shoulder.
Lower until the elbow lightly touches the floor.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the elbow off the floor
safety: Roll the bell into position from your side rather than lifting it overhead.
notes: Can also be done with two bells.

name: Bottoms-up kettlebell press
form_cues: Hold the bell upside down, crushing the handle.
Keep the wrist straight and bell balanced.
Press slowly straight up and lower with control.
common_mistakes: Loose grip causing the bell to tip
safety: Use a light bell; it can tip suddenly, so keep your head out of its path.

name: Kettlebell clean and press
form_cues: Clean the bell to the rack.
Pause, brace, and press overhead.
Lower to rack, then let it swing back for the next clean.
common_mistakes: Banging the forearm on the clean
safety: Keep the core braced throughout.

name: Kettlebell thruster
form_cues: Squat with the bell(s) in the rack.
Drive up out of the squat.
Use that momentum to press overhead.
safety: Keep heels down and lower the bells back to the rack under control.

name: Kettlebell high pull
form_cues: Start like a one-arm swing.
At the hip snap, pull the elbow back and high.
Let the bell return into the backswing.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arm too early
safety: Keep the bell close to avoid hitting your face.
notes: A teaching step toward the snatch.

name: Kettlebell sumo deadlift high pull
form_cues: Take a wide stance, bell between your feet.
Drive up through the legs and hips.
Pull the bell to chin height, elbows high.
common_mistakes: Pulling with arms before hips extend
safety: Avoid it if upright rows bother your shoulders.

name: Kettlebell front rack carry
form_cues: Clean two bells to the rack.
Walk tall with ribs down and short steps.
Breathe behind the brace.
safety: Set the bells down with a controlled hinge.
notes: Track distance in metres; one-bell version trains anti-side-bend.

name: Kettlebell overhead carry
form_cues: Press the bell overhead and lock the arm.
Keep the biceps by your ear while you walk.
Stay tall; don't lean away from the bell.
safety: Only carry overhead with full, pain-free shoulder mobility.

name: Kettlebell bent press
form_cues: Rack the bell and push the hip out to the side.
Lean under the bell while the arm stays vertical.
Stand up beneath the locked arm.
common_mistakes: Pressing the bell up instead of getting under it
safety: An advanced lift: learn it light and with coaching.
notes: Old-time strongman lift.

name: Weighted vest walking lunge
form_cues: Fit the vest snugly so it doesn't bounce.
Take a long step and lower the back knee softly.
Drive through the front heel into the next step.
safety: Start with a light vest (around 5–10% of body weight).
notes: Log the vest weight as added kg.

name: Weighted vest push-up
form_cues: Tighten the vest so the load sits high on the chest.
Keep a straight line from head to heels.
Lower until the chest nearly touches, then press up.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging under the extra load
safety: Add load gradually; reduce it if your lower back sags.
notes: Log vest weight as added kg.

name: Medicine ball push-up
form_cues: Place one hand on the ball, the other on the floor.
Lower with control, keeping hips square.
Press up and switch the ball to the other hand.
safety: Use a non-bouncing ball and keep the wrist stacked over it.

name: Medicine ball overhead lunge
form_cues: Hold the ball overhead with arms locked.
Step forward and lower the back knee.
Keep ribs down; don't let the ball drift forward.
safety: Skip the overhead hold if your shoulders lack mobility.

name: Medicine ball lunge with twist
form_cues: Hold the ball at chest height, arms extended.
Lunge forward, then rotate toward the front leg.
Turn back to centre before standing up.
common_mistakes: Front knee drifting inward when you rotate
safety: Rotate through the upper back, not the knee.

name: Medicine ball squat to press
form_cues: Hold the ball at your chest and squat.
Stand up and press the ball overhead.
Lower it to your chest as you sit back down.
safety: Control the ball overhead; don't release or throw it.

name: Sandbag bear-hug carry
form_cues: Hug the bag tight to your chest, hands clasped.
Stand tall and keep your chin over the bag.
Walk with short, quick steps and steady breathing.
safety: Lift the bag from the floor with a hinge, not a rounded back.

name: Sandbag clean
form_cues: Straddle the bag and grip the sides or handles.
Drive hips through to pop the bag up.
Drop under it and catch it on your forearms at the chest.
common_mistakes: Curling the bag up with the arms
safety: Start light; awkward loads need a tight, neutral spine.

name: Sandbag shouldering
form_cues: Lap the bag first by squatting and pulling it to your thighs.
Explode hips and pop the bag onto one shoulder.
Stand tall, then lower it under control.
common_mistakes: Lifting with the lower back alone
safety: A rounded back is normal on stone-style lifts but keep it braced; start light.

name: Sandbag Zercher squat
form_cues: Cradle the bag in the crooks of your elbows.
Squat deep while keeping the chest up.
Drive up through the whole foot.
safety: Keep elbows high and the load tight to your body.

name: Sandbag bear-hug squat
form_cues: Hug the bag tight to your chest.
Sit down between your knees.
Stand up without letting the bag pull you forward.
safety: Keep the bag close to reduce strain on the lower back.

name: Sandbag bent-over row
form_cues: Hinge forward with a flat back, holding the bag's handles.
Row the bag to your belly button.
Lower it slowly without losing your hinge.
safety: Keep the spine neutral and brace before each rep.

name: Sandbag overhead press
form_cues: Clean the bag to your chest.
Brace and press it straight overhead.
Lower it back to the chest under control.
safety: Use handles if available; loose sand shifts mid-rep.

name: Sandbag load to platform
form_cues: Lap the bag onto your thighs.
Hug it tight and extend the hips hard.
Drive the bag onto the platform without pressing it.
common_mistakes: Using the arms to throw the bag
Standing too far from the platform
safety: Use a stable platform at waist to chest height and keep fingers clear.
notes: Popular in strongman events and medleys.

name: Wrist roller
form_cues: Hold the roller at shoulder height with straight arms.
Roll the weight all the way up, one hand at a time.
Unroll slowly under control; don't let it drop.
common_mistakes: Letting arms drop to waist height
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain at the elbow (tennis-elbow area).
notes: Roll overhand for extensors and underhand for flexors.

name: Hand gripper squeeze
form_cues: Set the gripper deep in the palm.
Squeeze until the handles touch.
Hold the close for a second, then open slowly.
common_mistakes: Gripper set too high in the fingers
Rushing reps with no full close
safety: Build up gradually; overuse can irritate finger tendons.
notes: Hold for time at the close for crush endurance.

name: Finger extension with band
form_cues: Loop a band around all fingers and the thumb.
Spread fingers wide against the band.
Return slowly and repeat.
safety: Ease off if you feel joint pain.
notes: Balances out gripper and climbing work; helps keep elbows healthy.

name: Thick-grip dumbbell hold
form_cues: Fit thick grips over the handles.
Deadlift the dumbbells and stand tall.
Crush the handles and hold for time.
safety: Set the dumbbells down before your grip fully fails.

name: Thick-grip dumbbell curl
form_cues: Fit the thick grips and hold the dumbbells hard.
Curl up with elbows pinned to your sides.
Lower slowly without losing your crush grip.
safety: Use about 20–30% less weight than your normal curl.

name: Farmer's carry
form_cues: Deadlift the weights and stand tall.
Shoulders down and back, ribs stacked over hips.
Walk with short, quick steps; don't let weights swing.
safety: Lift and set the weights down with a flat back.
notes: Log weight per hand; a trap bar or farmer's handles allow heavier loads.

name: Suitcase carry
form_cues: Hold one weight at your side like a suitcase.
Stay perfectly upright; don't lean either way.
Walk slowly, then switch hands.
common_mistakes: Leaning away from or toward the weight
safety: Brace hard and pick the weight up with a hinge.

name: Plate pinch hold
form_cues: Pinch two smooth plates together, smooth sides out.
Keep fingers straight and thumb pressed hard.
Stand tall and hold for time.
safety: Hold over a clear floor and keep your feet out of the drop zone.
notes: Walk with the plates for a pinch carry.

name: Suspension row
form_cues: Lean back with arms straight and body in a plank.
Pull your chest to your hands, elbows at your sides.
Lower slowly, keeping hips up.
safety: Check the anchor point and straps before every set.
notes: Walk feet forward to make it harder.

name: Single-arm suspension row
form_cues: Hold both handles in one hand, body in a plank.
Row up without twisting toward the strap.
Lower slowly and keep hips square.
safety: Lock the handles together so they can't slip.

name: Suspension chest press
form_cues: Face away from the anchor, arms out in front.
Lower your chest between your hands in a plank.
Press back up without letting hips sag.
safety: Lower your body angle gradually; the straps can swing if you lose control.

name: Suspension chest fly
form_cues: Lean forward, arms out front with soft elbows.
Open arms wide as you lower your chest.
Hug back together using your chest.
common_mistakes: Going too low and straining shoulders
safety: Start upright and only lean further once you control the bottom.

name: Suspension bicep curl
form_cues: Face the anchor, palms up, leaning back.
Keep elbows high and still.
Curl hands toward your forehead.
safety: Walk feet forward slowly to add load.

name: Suspension triceps extension
form_cues: Face away, arms straight overhead holding handles.
Bend only at the elbows, hands toward your forehead.
Straighten arms to push back to the start.
safety: Begin fairly upright; the movement gets hard quickly as you lean.

name: Suspension Y raise
form_cues: Lean back with straight arms.
Raise arms up and out into a Y shape.
Keep shoulders down, away from ears.
safety: Use a small lean; this targets small muscles.
notes: Pair with T and W raises as a shoulder-health circuit.

name: Suspension reverse fly
form_cues: Lean back, arms straight in front.
Open arms wide into a T.
Squeeze shoulder blades, then return slowly.
safety: Keep the lean modest at first.

name: Suspension face pull
form_cues: Lean back, palms down, arms straight.
Pull elbows high and wide, hands beside your ears.
Finish in a W shape, then lower slowly.
safety: Keep it pain-free in the shoulder.

name: Suspension-assisted pistol squat
form_cues: Hold the handles and stand on one leg.
Sit down slowly with the free leg out front.
Use the straps only as much as needed to rise.
safety: Stop above the depth where your knee or hip hurts.
notes: Reduce the arm assist over time.

name: Suspension lunge
form_cues: Place the back foot in the foot cradle.
Lower the back knee toward the floor.
Drive through the front heel to stand.
safety: Lower the straps to mid-calf height for good balance.

name: Suspension hamstring curl
form_cues: Lie on your back with heels in the cradles.
Lift hips into a bridge.
Curl heels to your glutes, keeping hips high.
safety: Set the straps about 20–30 cm off the floor.

name: Suspension hip press
form_cues: Lie on your back, heels in the cradles.
Press heels down and lift hips high.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
safety: Keep the straps still before lifting.

name: Ring row
form_cues: Hang under the rings, body straight.
Pull the rings to your ribs, turning palms in.
Lower to straight arms with control.
safety: Check ring straps and anchor before use.
notes: Raise the feet on a box to make it harder.

name: Ring push-ups
form_cues: Set rings a few centimetres off the floor.
Lower with elbows tucked and rings steady.
Press up and turn the rings out at the top.
safety: Set rings low first so a slip doesn't drop you far.

name: Ring bicep curl
form_cues: Lean back with palms up and arms straight.
Curl hands toward your forehead, elbows high.
Lower slowly without dropping elbows.
safety: Rings rotate freely, so start with a small lean.

name: Ring fly
form_cues: Start in a push-up position on the rings.
Slide arms wide with a slight elbow bend.
Squeeze arms back together under the chest.
safety: Start rings high and feet close to keep the load manageable; deep stretches strain the shoulder.

name: Yoke carry
form_cues: Set under the yoke bar like a back squat.
Brace hard and stand it up.
Take short, fast steps, keeping the yoke level.
common_mistakes: Taking long strides that swing the yoke
Losing the brace and folding forward
safety: Learn with light loads on a flat surface and drop the yoke forward or back if you lose control.
notes: No yoke? A barbell in a rack can be walked out for short distances (bar walk). req uses barbell as nearest gear id.

name: Sled push
form_cues: Grip the poles with arms long and lean in at 45 degrees.
Drive knees forward and push through the balls of the feet.
Keep your back flat and steps powerful.
safety: Use a clear lane and a surface the sled slides evenly on.
notes: No eccentric load, so it is easy to recover from.

name: Sled rope pull
form_cues: Sit or stand in an athletic stance holding the rope.
Pull hand over hand, keeping the sled moving.
Brace your core and don't round your back.
safety: Clear the rope path and keep fingers out of the sled hardware.

name: Backward sled drag
form_cues: Hold the straps facing the sled, arms long.
Sit slightly and walk backward on the balls of your feet.
Keep tension in the straps and take steady steps.
safety: Check the path behind you is clear before you start.
notes: Knee-friendly quad builder; often used for rehab.

name: Forward sled drag
form_cues: Clip the harness or hold the straps behind you.
Lean forward and drive each leg back powerfully.
Keep a tall spine and steady pace.
common_mistakes: Leaning too far and losing balance
safety: Use a harness that sits at the waist or chest, not the neck.

name: Tyre flip
form_cues: Squat down, chest against the tyre, fingers under the tread.
Drive forward and up with the legs, not the arms.
Pop a knee in, flip hands, and push it over.
common_mistakes: Curling the tyre with the arms (biceps tear risk)
safety: Keep arms long (never curl the tyre) and stay clear of where it lands.
notes: No gear id for a tyre; req uses sled as the nearest strongman-area id.

name: Atlas stone load
form_cues: Straddle the stone and wrap your arms deep around it.
Lap it onto your thighs, then re-grip high.
Extend hips explosively to roll it onto the platform.
common_mistakes: Stone too far from the body
safety: Use tacky and forearm sleeves, start light, and keep your feet clear of the drop.
notes: No gear id for stones; req uses sandbag, the closest home substitute.

name: Log press
form_cues: Clean the log onto your chest, elbows high.
Dip and drive with the legs.
Press through to lockout with the head forward.
safety: Learn the clean light and drop the log in front, never behind you.
notes: No log gear id; req uses barbell as nearest. Neutral grip suits sore shoulders.

name: Axle deadlift
equipment: Axle bar or barbell with thick grips
form_cues: Set up like a normal deadlift, double overhand grip.
Squeeze the thick bar hard before you pull.
Drive through the floor and lock out tall.
common_mistakes: Mixed grip to avoid grip work
Bar drifting away from the shins
safety: Use a hook or double overhand grip and lower with control; the axle doesn't spin.
notes: Thick grips on a regular barbell mimic an axle.
